answer: Neighborhood wedge quota: each node may hold at most k active links to neighbors whose own neighbor sets overlap above a threshold. Because fake identities must interconnect to act, they form a dense terrace in graph space, and any vertex joining it inherits high overlap. The signal is purely the adjacency structure, checked at edge admission. Enforcement: links exceeding k are refused, so an attacker must spread clones across many sparse regions, paying real latency and connectivity costs per identity to keep overlap low.
